paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the change in loss over training time for two different models. The x-axis is labeled "Training Time (s)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds, with tick intervals at every 50,000 seconds. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick intervals of 0.05. There are two lines in the plot. The first line, labeled "Vanilla", is represented by a purple color with triangular markers and a solid line style. It starts at a loss value of approximately 2.75 at slightly more than 0 seconds and decreases to about 2.50 just before 250,000 seconds, showing a consistent downward trend. The second line, labeled "SepLLM", is depicted in red with circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at a similar initial loss value around 2.75 at slightly more than 0 seconds and trends downward to approximately 2.48 just before the red line around 240,000 seconds, also showing a steady decrease over time. Both lines show a general reduction in loss as the training time increases, with specific decreases noted along the axis. The red line is always below the purple line. There's a green dashed line along the x-axis at loss of 2.5, which intercepts the red line and ends at end of purple line, and is marked in a green star. From these intercepts, two other green dashed line, perpendicular to the x-axis is given, these lines are of height Loss 2.56. And between these two lines, at the top, a green line parallel the x-axis is there, and a text "1.26x" is given on top. A legend is given top right.
